vt.analysis:
Package: vector-memory (mcp)
Version: 2.1.1
Description: Smart memory search with automatic vector fallback. Uses semantic embeddings when available, falls back to built-in search otherwise. Zero configuration - works immediately after install.

The package provides a local vector-based memory search system for the OpenClaw agent framework. It utilizes the Transformers.js library to generate embeddings locally using the all-MiniLM-L6-v2 model, enabling semantic search capabilities without external API calls. The codebase includes a smart wrapper (smart_memory.js) that automatically switches between neural vector search and a keyword-based fallback search depending on the availability of the index. It manages memory files within a specific workspace directory, implements semantic chunking, and provides a CLI for indexing and searching. No malicious behavior, unauthorized data exfiltration, or suspicious network activity was detected; the installation script and file operations are consistent with the stated purpose of an agent skill extension.

llm.summary: This memory-search skill is mostly purpose-aligned, but it contains unsafe command execution and file-reading flaws that could expose local files or run unintended commands.

dimensions.detail: Local model download, workspace cache use, and vector index writes are coherent for semantic search, but arbitrary shell execution and path traversal exceed the minimum authority needed for memory lookup.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The documentation and installer include curl-to-bash and mutable GitHub main-branch install flows, then run npm install without a lockfile or exact dependency pinning.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill exposes shell command templates and smart_memory.js passes interpolated query and max_results values into execSync string commands, creating command-injection risk if crafted inputs reach the tool.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill writes a persistent vector index and model cache under the OpenClaw workspace and suggests optional heartbeat/cron auto-sync; no backdoor, service install, or hidden persistence was found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is local semantic memory search, and reading/indexing memory files fits that purpose; however, memory_get joins caller-controlled paths without containment checks, allowing reads outside intended memory files.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. The local semantic-memory goal is understandable, but install only from a trusted, pinned source; avoid the curl | bash path; and fix or wait for fixes to command execution and file path containment before using it on a workspace with secrets or sensitive files.
llm.findings:
[TM2] unexpected: The pipe-to-shell installer is present in README.md, skills/vector-memory/README.md, and install.sh comments; this is not necessary for the memory-search purpose and materially weakens install safety.
[TP4] expected: The zero-configuration claim is partly supported by smart_memory.js fallback behavior, but install.sh performs dependency installation and initial sync, and first vector sync downloads a model; this is under-disclosed rather than deceptive.
[AE1] expected: The referenced JavaScript artifacts are present in this workspace and were inspected, so the partial-inspection concern is overridden for this adjudication.
[RP1] unexpected: Unpinned npx/GitHub/dependency flows are confirmed and create supply-chain risk, though they do not show malicious intent by themselves.
[LP3] unexpected: The manifest relies on broad shell command strings for tool execution and does not express tight scoping around the commands or file paths.
[SDI-1] expected: smart_memory.js implements fallback search, while memory.js is less complete; the mismatch is a quality/disclosure issue, not evidence of a hidden unrelated capability.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The path traversal in memory_get and unsafe installer examples are artifact-backed concerns that exceed a narrowly scoped memory retrieval tool.
[SQP-1] expected: The trigger language is broad but still centered on memory search and does not by itself create a material security concern.
[SDI-4] expected: Package and manifest descriptions are not perfectly aligned, but both describe local vector memory functionality.
[T03] unexpected: Remote mutable source retrieval and pipe-to-shell installation were confirmed in the artifact and are not required for safe installation.
[T09] unexpected: The execSync string construction with caller-controlled query/max_results is confirmed and can enable command injection.
[T05] unexpected: The memory_get path handling permits workspace escape and arbitrary readable-file disclosure, which is broader than retrieving memory files.
[T08] expected: External npm and model dependencies are expected for local embeddings, but lack of exact pinning, lockfile, and project-level model integrity checks should be reviewed before installation.
